testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: The test 'a sibling key with no checkout-path, one holding a relative path, or one whose path does not hash to the key's suffix is kept' does not discriminate the `!isAbsolute(line)` or the multi-line `line.includes("\n")` guard in checkoutOf: its relative-path and two-line fixtures are named with suffixes that do not hash their content, so the hash check catches them and the guards are never reached.
survived.evidence: red: n/a, both mutants survived. m2 (drop `!isAbsolute(line)`): `./agent-test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76 fail 0. m3 (drop `line.includes("\n")`): same command → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76 fail 0. baseline: `./agent-test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76, the named test passes. Contrast m1 (drop the hash check) → exit 1, fail 1 incl that same test.
survived.suggested_fix: Build the relative-path and two-line fixtures so the key name's 8-hex suffix is the sha256 prefix of that exact content, then assert the reason is `holds no single absolute path`. The assertion is currently only /^no checkout file: /, so it also cannot tell the branches apart.

votes.reason: I ran both mutants in my own copy of the snapshot. Each replaced line 587 of plugin/scripts/reclaim-scratch.mjs so that only one of the two guards remained. With only `line.includes("\n")` kept (the `!isAbsolute` guard dropped), `./agent-test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs` exited 0 with tests 76, pass 76, fail 0. With only `!isAbsolute(line)` kept (the multi-line guard dropped), the same command gave tests 76, pass 76, fail 0. I did not run an unmutated baseline or the drop-the-hash-check mutant myself, so the baseline and m1 contrast are as the claim reports them. I did not read the `f.key` fixture helper. Reading the test showed the relative-path fixture uses the arbitrary suffix `relative-22222222`, and the two-line fixture takes the default suffix. The default suffix presumably hashes `checkout` rather than the two-line content (not verified), so the hash check at line 589 rejects both fixtures and the guards are never needed. The test only asserts the reason matches /^no checkout file: /, so it cannot tell which guard fired. The mutation was reverted from a backup copy. unverified.claim: The rule that keeps a key when the directory that held its checkout is also gone (meant for unplugged drives) fails for a checkout at a volume's mount root. If checkout-path names /Volumes/<Drive>, the drive is unplugged and /Volumes exists, the whole key, including its pr<N> partitions, is removed under --apply.
unverified.evidence: Fake HOME, ws repo, key `UnpluggedDrive-$(printf %s /Volumes/UnpluggedDrive | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8)` holding checkout-path `/Volumes/UnpluggedDrive` and pr9/run-1/review.json, everything touched to 2026-10-01. Running `node reclaim-scratch.mjs --siblings --root $ROOT --apply` printed `"removed":[{"path":".../UnpluggedDrive-234f3b03","reason":"its checkout /Volumes/UnpluggedDrive is gone and nothing under it changed in 7 days"}]`.
unverified.suggested_fix: The ruling chose the parent-directory test, so this is a gap in the ruling's own unplugged-drive reasoning. It is not a deviation from the brief. Raise it with the maintainer, for example: also keep a key when dirname(checkout) is a known mount parent (/Volumes, /media/*, /mnt), or when the held directory sits on a different st_dev from its own parent.

unverified.claim: checkoutOf() calls readFileSync on a sibling key's checkout-path without first checking that it is a regular file. A FIFO there blocks the sibling pass forever, and a symlink to a device such as /dev/zero would read without end. phase0's reclaim step spawns the pass with no timeout, so every phase 0 on the machine would hang.
unverified.evidence: Ran `mkfifo $PARENT/fifo-aaaaaaaa/checkout-path`, then `perl -e 'alarm 10; exec @ARGV' node reclaim-scratch.mjs --siblings --root $ROOT`, which printed `exit=142` (killed by SIGALRM after 10.27s; it never returned). In phase0.mjs:435-437, `node("reclaim-scratch.mjs", ["--siblings", ...], { cwd })` passes no timeoutMs.
unverified.suggested_fix: Call lstatSync first and treat anything that is not a regular file, or is larger than a few KB, as `{ none }`. Alternatively, open with O_NONBLOCK and run fstat before reading.

unverified.claim: No test checks that existsAt uses lstat, which the brief requires. Swapping lstatSync for statSync leaves both test files green, so a dangling symlink at a checkout path would silently count as 'gone'.
unverified.evidence: Mutation M6 (`lstatSync(p);` changed to `statSync(p);` in existsAt), then `node --test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs`: exit 0, no failing tests.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a fixture whose checkout path is a dangling symlink and assert the key is kept with the 'still exists' reason.

unverified.claim: No test checks that an unreadable checkout-path (EACCES/EPERM) counts as 'no checkout file', as the brief rules. Removing EACCES and EPERM from NO_CHECKOUT_FILE leaves the suite green, and only the kept reason changes.
unverified.evidence: Mutation M7 (NO_CHECKOUT_FILE reduced to ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EISDIR), then `node --test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs`: exit 0, no failing tests.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a non-root fixture that chmods a sibling's checkout-path to 000 and asserts a reason matching /^no checkout file: checkout-path cannot be read \(EACCES\)/.

unverified.claim: A failed write of the live key's checkout-path is put in failed[] and surfaced by phase0 as 'sibling keys: could not reclaim <key>/checkout-path (<error>)'. The unreclaimed() helper hardcodes the verb 'reclaim', so this write failure is mislabelled as a reclaim failure. The error text also names the temp file '.checkout-path.<pid>.tmp', not 'checkout-path'.
unverified.evidence: Probe: chmod 555 on the live root, then `reclaim-scratch.mjs --siblings --root $ROOT --apply` printed exit 0 and failed:[{"path":".../repo-a9fa9a49/checkout-path","error":"EACCES: permission denied, open '.../.checkout-path.9371.tmp'"}]. phase0.mjs:441 passes that receipt to unreclaimed('sibling keys', siblings, {named:true}), whose line 170 maps every failed[] entry to `could not ${verb} ${path} (${error})` with verb='reclaim'. I read that mapping but did not run phase0 itself.
unverified.suggested_fix: Make the failed[] error for this case self-describing, for example 'could not record checkout-path: <message>', or let writeCheckout's entry carry a verb that phase0 uses. The signal is not lost, only mislabelled.

unverified.claim: The guard against removing a key whose checkout sits on an unplugged drive only covers the case where the checkout's parent directory is also gone (macOS /Volumes/X). Where the drive's mount point stays behind as an empty directory (for example /mnt/data), the checkout is gone while its parent is present. The key then reads as 'gone, parent present' and is removed whole after 7 idle days.
unverified.evidence: Probe: key whose checkout-path names $D/w/held/gone1, with $D/w/held an existing empty directory, backdated 2020. The `--siblings --apply` receipt put it in removed[] with reason 'its checkout ... is gone and nothing under it changed in 7 days'. Not run: an actual unmounted drive. That a mount point survives unmounting is inferred.
unverified.suggested_fix: Accept this as a documented limit, or also keep a key when the held directory is empty or is a mount point. The behaviour is by design for the macOS case, but the docs say 'an unplugged drive reads the same', which overstates the protection.

unverified.claim: Keys with no valid checkout-path are kept forever and are never aged out. This includes every pre-existing key from before this change, and any key whose workspace never ran a phase 0 with the new code. Their reason string is 'no checkout file: ...' and they are shown with idle:true on every phase 0 pass. Orphaned legacy keys therefore accumulate silently on disk, with a recurring note in phase-0 output but no path to removal.
unverified.evidence: Probe and diff test: a key with checkout-path missing is kept with reason 'no checkout file: checkout-path is missing' and idle:true. The diff's removed test '(11) a sibling key with nothing modified in 7 days is removed' confirms the old age-only removal is gone. Not run: any long-term accumulation.
unverified.suggested_fix: Decide explicitly whether legacy keys should age out. If so, add a fallback for a key with no file, such as a longer retention. Otherwise record the intent in the ADR as a known cost.

unverified.claim: The unreadable-error paths in checkoutOf, existsAt and judgeSibling have no coverage that discriminates: the 'error' (non-NO_CHECKOUT_FILE read failure) branch, the EPERM entry in NO_CHECKOUT_FILE, the ENOTDIR case in existsAt, and the `up instanceof Error` and `at instanceof Error` keep branches can each be deleted with the suite staying green.
unverified.evidence: All with `./agent-test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76 fail 0: m17 (drop `found.error` return), m11 (drop EPERM from NO_CHECKOUT_FILE), m13 (drop ENOTDIR from existsAt), m14 (`up instanceof Error` → false), m15 (`at instanceof Error` → false). baseline: the same command on the unmutated tree → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76. These are fail-safe branches whose job is to keep a key when the state is unknown, so a regression there would silently remove a live key. Tests would need a fault-injecting stub or an unreadable parent dir.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a test where the checkout's parent is unreadable (chmod 000, skipped under root) and one where checkout-path is a directory or unreadable, asserting the key is kept with the 'cannot be told' / 'cannot be read' reason.

unverified.claim: The writeCheckout failure path does not assert that the temp file is cleaned up: removing the `rmSync(tmp, {force:true})` cleanup leaves every test green.
unverified.evidence: m16 (replace `rmSync(tmp, { force: true });` with a comment): `./agent-test tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76 fail 0. baseline: same command unmutated → exit 0, tests 76 pass 76. The failing-write test chmods the key read-only, so no temp file is ever created and the cleanup cannot matter there.
unverified.suggested_fix: Make the failure occur at rename (for example a directory named checkout-path, so renameSync fails) and assert no `.checkout-path.*.tmp` remains.

unverified.claim: The research table row says `--siblings` 'removes other key-shaped roots idle 7 days', which the PR changed to checkout-gone plus idle.
unverified.evidence: docs/research/run-artifacts.md:96 reads '(4) `--siblings` (`phase0.mjs:356`) removes other *key-shaped* roots idle 7 days'. The diff makes removal depend on the recorded checkout-path being gone, its parent present and the key idle. The file is a dated research snapshot, so the line is arguably historical.
unverified.suggested_fix: Update the row or leave it, given the file's dated status.

unverified.claim: checkoutOf returns an untagged union ({none}|{error}|{checkout}) that callers discriminate by testing which property is !== undefined. Nothing prevents an object with several of these keys. The shape is documented only in a comment.
unverified.evidence: Read lines 575-632. judgeSibling checks `found.error !== undefined`, then `found.none !== undefined`, then destructures `checkout`. The only consumer today is judgeSibling, and each return site sets exactly one key, so there is no live bug.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add an explicit discriminant such as `{kind:'checkout'|'none'|'error', ...}`, or a JSDoc @typedef union, so the three cases are exclusive and checkable.

unverified.claim: existsAt returns boolean | Error, and callers branch on `instanceof Error` before testing truthiness. Swapping those two checks would silently treat an unknown state as 'exists'. Nothing but ordering enforces the ordering.
unverified.evidence: Lines 606-626: `if (at instanceof Error) ... ; if (at) ...` and the same pattern for `up`. The order is correct today.
unverified.suggested_fix: Return a tri-state string ('exists'|'absent') or `{error}`, so that truthiness can't conflate the cases.

unverified.claim: The `idle` field on kept[] entries is optional: only sibling-pass entries carry it, and root-sweep entries omit it. The consumer in phase0.mjs depends on `x?.idle === true`, so the receipt shape is documented in a comment but not enforced. Kept entries from the two passes have different shapes.
unverified.evidence: Line 566 and the re-judge at ~line 757 push `{path, reason, idle}`. The phase0.mjs `unreclaimed` change filters `kept.filter((x) => x?.idle === true)` and does a runtime Array.isArray check on removed and kept. The comment in reclaim-scratch.mjs says kept carries idle only for the sibling pass.
unverified.suggested_fix: Give every kept[] entry an explicit boolean `idle` (false for the root sweep) so the shape is uniform, or add a shared typedef for the receipt entry.

unverified.claim: checkoutOf() repeats the key-hash rule inline (`createHash("sha256").update(line).digest("hex").startsWith(suffix)`), and fleet-dir.mjs:160's scratchRoot() has its own copy (`createHash("sha256").update(dir).digest("hex").slice(0, 8)`), so the rule that names a key and the rule that validates its checkout-path can drift apart.
unverified.evidence: In the scratch copy I added `export function scratchKeyHex(dir) { return createHash("sha256").update(dir).digest("hex").slice(0, 8); }` to fleet-dir.mjs and used it in scratchRoot() (`const hex = scratchKeyHex(dir)`). In checkoutOf I used `if (scratchKeyHex(line) !== suffix)`, and dropped reclaim-scratch's createHash import. `===` gives the same result as `startsWith` because SCRATCH_KEY_SHAPE (/-[0-9a-f]{8}$/) guarantees `basename(key).slice(-8)` is exactly 8 lowercase hex characters for every judged key and for the live root. Result: `node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs tests/fleet-dir.test.mjs tests/fleet-dir-layouts.test.mjs tests/scratch-root.test.mjs`, tests 123, pass 123, fail 0. That run includes the mismatch-suffix test ('a sibling key with no checkout-path, one holding a relative path, or one whose path does not hash…') and the scratch-root hash tests.
unverified.suggested_fix: Export one `scratchKeyHex(dir)` from fleet-dir.mjs beside SCRATCH_KEY_SHAPE. Use it in scratchRoot() and in checkoutOf (`if (scratchKeyHex(line) !== suffix) return …`), and remove the createHash import from reclaim-scratch.mjs.

unverified.claim: checkoutOf() returns three result shapes (`{checkout}`, `{none}`, `{error}`), but both callers treat `none` and `error` the same way: judgeSibling keeps the key in both cases and only adds a `no checkout file: ` prefix to `none`, and writeCheckout only tests `.checkout`. So checkoutOf could return the final reason itself and drop one branch and one result field.
unverified.evidence: In the scratch copy, checkoutOf returns `{ reason: `no checkout file: ${…}` }` for every former `none` case and `{ reason: `its ${CHECKOUT_FILE} cannot be read: ${e.message}` }` for the former `error` case. judgeSibling's two lines (`if (found.error !== undefined) return keep(found.error); if (found.none !== undefined) return keep(`no checkout file: ${found.none}`);`) became `if (found.reason !== undefined) return keep(found.reason);`. Every reason string stays byte-identical. Result: the same targeted TAP run, 123/123 pass, including the tests that check kept reasons against /^no checkout file: / and the exact checkout-path write/rewrite tests.
unverified.suggested_fix: function checkoutOf(key) → `{ checkout }` | `{ reason }`, where `reason` is the full keep reason: `no checkout file: checkout-path is missing`, `no checkout file: checkout-path cannot be read (EACCES)`, `its checkout-path cannot be read: <msg>`, and so on. In judgeSibling: `if (found.reason !== undefined) return keep(found.reason);`. Update the comment above checkoutOf to describe the two shapes.

unverified.claim: judgeSibling's final `return { remove: true, …, idle }` passes a variable that can only be `true` there, because the line just before it, `if (!idle) return keep(…)`, has already returned whenever idle is false. Writing `idle: true` says this directly.
unverified.evidence: Control flow at snapshot lines 627-629: `if (!idle) return keep("sibling key modified within 7 days"); if (unreadable.length > 0) return keep(…); return { remove: true, reason: …, idle };`. In the scratch copy I replaced the last field with `idle: true`. Result: the same targeted TAP run, 123/123 pass. Also, judgeSiblings (line 565) and main's recheck (line 756) never read `idle` from a verdict with remove:true. They push `{path, reason}` to remove[] or `continue` past it, so the field is unread on that path either way.
unverified.suggested_fix: `return { remove: true, reason: `its checkout ${checkout} is gone and nothing under it changed in 7 days` };`, dropping `idle` because no caller reads it when remove is true. If the verdict should keep one uniform shape, write `idle: true` instead.
